newsitem.title: PERU: Peru tax body sees '96 revs up 5.5 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Peru tax body sees '96 revs up 5.5 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Peru's National Superintendency of Tax Administration (SUNAT) said Wednesday it estimated this year's tax revenues would total 19.717 billion soles, 5.5 percent higher in real terms than tax revenue in 1995.
The SUNAT also estimated December's revenues would be 1.609 billion soles, up 1.0 percent in real terms compared with the same month last year, the tax body added in a statement.

Earlier this month, SUNAT said cumulative revenues for the first eleven months of 1996 were 18.1 billion soles, up 5.7 percent compared with the same period last year after taking into account inflation.
Tax collection last year rose 27.7 percent in nominal terms to 17.063 billion soles, from 13.363 billion soles in 1994.
Peru's cumulative consumer inflation in the 12-month period up to the end of November this year was 11.9 percent.
